newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air Q1 oper expenses up 2.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air Q1 oper expenses up 2.6 pct.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co said higher jet fuel costs and increased profit-sharing and employee savings plan contributions pushed first quarter operating expenses higher.
Lower aircraft engine overhaul costs partially offset those cost increases, the company said.
First quarter operating expenses per available seat mile increased 2.6 percent to $0.0761, compared to $0.0742 last year.

"We were extremely pleased with our first quarter 1997 unit cost performance. Excluding fuel, our operating costs per ASM were flat with last year," said Herbert Kelleher, Southwest chairman and chief executive. "Fortunately, fuel prices have now receded from first quarter 1997 levels."
Revenue passenger miles (RPMs) increased 11.9 percent in first quarter 1997, while available seat miles (ASMs) increased 9.1 percent.

The passenger revenue yield per RPM increased 2.4 percent to $0.1300 from $0.1270 in first quarter 1996. Operating revenue yield per ASM increased 5.2 percent to $0.0843 from $0.0801 in first quarter 1996.
First quarter load factor was 62.1 percent, compared to 60.5 percent last year.
The Dallas-based airline earned $0.34 a share or $50.8 million on total operating revenues of $887.1 million in the first quarter, topping the consensus Wall Street estimate of $0.23 a share.
During the first quarter last year, Southwest earned $0.22 a share or $33.0 million on total operating revenues of $772.5 million.
Southwest said it ended the first quarter with $652.4 million in cash plus an available and unused bank credit line of $460.0 million.
